events.text: The first snow of the year comes in the night, without a sound. By morning the valley is white and every track is written down. A hare went this way. A fox went after it. A man with one boot heavier than the other went nowhere in particular.

choices.text: Go out and read every track

effects.log: By noon you know who lives within a day of you, and who is limping. The man with the heavy boot was looking for something. He did not find it.

choices.text: Stay where you are and watch it fall

effects.log: You watch until the snow fills your own tracks too. It is very quiet. For a whole day nothing in the world wants anything from you.

choices.text: Leave no tracks at all, as a game

ok.log: You keep to the rocks and the roots all day. In the evening a hunter stands where you stood and scratches his head.

fail.log: The rock is ice under the snow. You go down hard and lie there, laughing at yourself, if that is the word for it.

events.text: Two magpies in the persimmon tree have decided you are a problem. They have told every bird in the valley. Now there are eleven magpies, all shouting, and a crow who came to see what the fuss was about.

choices.text: Ignore them until they get bored

effects.log: They do not get bored. You do. But you learn to sit inside the noise like a stone in a stream, and that is worth something.

choices.text: Lunge at the tree, once

effects.log: Every bird leaves at once. The persimmon tree shakes off three ripe fruit. The magpies will be back tomorrow. So will the fruit.

choices.text: Move somewhere quieter

effects.log: You find a hollow under a fallen pine. It is quiet. It is also full of ants. Somewhere the magpies are telling the story of how they won.

events.text: A hunting party goes up the valley with dogs and bows. The youngest, a boy of maybe eight, falls behind to pick a mushroom and loses the voices. He turns round and round. Then he sees you, and stops turning.

choices.text: Stay perfectly still and let him look

effects.log: He looks for a long time. Then he whispers something, maybe a greeting, maybe a prayer, and backs away very carefully. He will tell this story at seventy.

choices.text: Slip away before he can shout

effects.log: When he blinks you are gone. He finds the voices on his own, and when he tells his father, his father laughs. The boy does not.

choices.text: Move slowly toward the voices so he follows

effects.log: You keep just ahead of him, a rustle here, a shadow there, until he hears the dogs. He runs to his father. He does not look back, which is wise of him.

events.text: There is a carp in the pond under the ice, old and gold and very slow. The village says a carp that swims up the falls becomes a dragon. This one has never tried. It hangs under the ice all winter, looking up at you.

choices.text: Watch it all winter

effects.log: By spring you think you understand it. It is not lazy. It is waiting for a reason. That is not the same thing.

choices.text: Tap the ice to see what it does

effects.log: It does nothing. It has seen everything. You feel faintly judged by a fish.

choices.text: Sleep beside the pond so it has company

effects.log: When the ice breaks, it rises and opens its mouth at you, once. Then it goes back down. It is the most a carp will say.

events.text: It is the end of winter, the worst part. The cold has eaten everything. Your hunger has a shape now, and it follows you around like a dog. The village below has smoke in every chimney and a full storehouse.

choices.text: Range far past your usual ground to find food

ok.log: Three valleys away you find what you need. You come home thinner but full, and you know three more valleys.

fail.log: You range far and find less than you spent getting there. You come home with the hunger walking even closer.

choices.text: Sleep through it

effects.log: You sleep, and wake, and sleep. The hunger waits by the door. In the end the spring comes and it gets bored and leaves.

choices.text: Go down to the village stores

effects.log: The stores are lighter by morning. The village is awake all night with torches and drums. By morning there is a new story about you, and men at the edge of the woods.

events.text: You lie down in autumn to rest for a few days. When you wake it is spring, the sapling beside you has put out new leaves, and someone has built a fence at the bottom of the hill. You are not sure how many days that was.

choices.text: Count the rings of a fallen branch

effects.log: One ring since you lay down. One winter. You feel you should have noticed something. You did not.

choices.text: Go and look at the fence

effects.log: It is a good fence. It is around a field of millet. The field is around a house. The house has a child in it. You wonder when it was built.

choices.text: Go back to sleep

effects.log: You wake again in spring. The sapling is taller. You decide this is how you will tell time from now on.

events.text: Blue fires come bobbing down the mountain road at midnight, laughing. Dokkaebi. One of them, big and hairy with a knobbed club, plants itself in front of you. It wants to wrestle. It has wanted to wrestle all night and nobody will.

choices.text: Wrestle it

ok.log: You throw it. It sits in the road, delighted, and the others howl. At dawn it turns into an old broom, which explains a lot.

fail.log: It throws you three times. Dokkaebi do not tire. At dawn it turns into a broom and you are still lying in the road.

choices.text: Throw it from the left, as the old stories say

effects.log: Dokkaebi have no strength on the left. Over it goes. It complains it was a trick. It was. It comes back the next night for another.

choices.text: Ignore it and go on

effects.log: It follows you for a mile, shouting challenges. Then it finds a drunk farmer on the road and you hear the poor man yelling till dawn.

events.text: The cranes come back to the river flats, red-crowned, in pairs. You count them every year. This year there are thirty-one. Last year there were thirty-four. You find that you mind.

choices.text: Watch them dance

effects.log: They bow and leap and throw their heads back. It looks ridiculous. You watch the whole morning.

choices.text: Look for the three that did not come

effects.log: You do not find them. You find a net in the reeds, rotten now. You remember it.

choices.text: Keep watch on the flats for them

effects.log: Nothing bothers the cranes that winter. They do not know why. They do not need to.

events.text: A pilgrim crosses the pass and stops at the cairn. She takes a rice ball from her bundle, sets it on a flat stone, bows to the mountain spirit, and goes on. The mountain spirit is not here today. You are.

choices.text: Eat it

effects.log: It is cold and salted and has a pickled plum in the middle. You understand, for the first time, why the mountain spirit keeps this pass.

choices.text: Leave it for the spirit

effects.log: By evening a crow has eaten it. The crow, you suspect, is also not the mountain spirit.

choices.text: Follow the pilgrim down a little way

effects.log: She sings to herself on the road, badly, the same song again and again. You keep pace with her to the tree line and turn back.

events.text: Men are burning the forest on the far slope to make a fire-field. The smoke rolls over the ridge. The animals come past you in a line, deer, a badger, a family of boar, not looking at each other.

choices.text: Go with them, away from the smoke

effects.log: You spend a week in the next valley with the deer and the boar. Nobody eats anybody. Fire is a strange peace.

choices.text: Stay and watch the burning

effects.log: Your eyes sting all day. You watch the men work the fire with wet branches. They are good at it. That frightens you more than the fire.

choices.text: Wait for the rain and come back after

effects.log: In two years there is millet where the forest was. In ten the soil is tired and they move on. In thirty it is forest again.

events.text: The summer rains come and do not stop. Forty days. The streams are brown and loud. Everything around you is wet, which is to say you are wet. The frogs are delighted. Nobody else is.

choices.text: Find high ground and wait it out

effects.log: You wait. It rains. You wait. On the forty-first day the sun comes out and the whole valley steams like a pot.

choices.text: Watch the stream change its shape

effects.log: The stream cuts a new bend in a single night. You realise every river you know was made like this, one bad summer at a time.

choices.text: Go out in it anyway

effects.log: You get very wet and very cold and learn nothing except that rain does not care about you. That is a lesson.

events.text: Three village children creep up the slope, daring each other. Whoever gets closest to where the monster lives wins. The smallest has a stick. The biggest is at the back.

choices.text: Let the smallest one win

effects.log: You shift a little, so she sees an eye. She shrieks and runs, and wins forever. The biggest one will never live it down.

choices.text: Make one low sound

effects.log: They leave so fast one of them loses a shoe. The shoe stays on the slope for a year. Nobody comes back for it.

choices.text: Keep still and let them lose interest

effects.log: They creep, they whisper, they argue, and then someone's mother calls them for dinner. The monster is no match for dinner.

events.text: The ginseng diggers come up the mountain in odd numbers, washed and fasting, so the mountain will not be offended. They search all day on their knees. Near sunset one of them shouts "Simbatta!" and the others fall silent.

choices.text: Watch them dig it out with deer-bone picks

effects.log: They take an hour over one root, so as not to break a single hair. You have never seen humans so patient. It does not last past the root.

choices.text: Show them the old root they missed

effects.log: A branch moves, and one of them looks where it points. A second root, older. The old digger bows to the empty forest for a long time.

choices.text: Keep the oldest roots hidden

effects.log: There is a root up here older than the village. You lie across that slope all evening. They go home with one, and they are happy.

events.text: The path you take every night has changed. The leaves lie too flat. The ground smells of fresh earth and of men. Someone has dug a pit and lined it with sharpened stakes, right where you always step.

choices.text: Step around it

ok.log: You go around. In the morning the hunters find their pit empty and argue about whose fault it is.

fail.log: The second pit was beside the first. You get out, but the stakes go deep, and the wounds take a season to close.

choices.text: Fill it in, a little each night

effects.log: Every morning the hunters dig it out. Every night it is filled. By the end of the month they say the mountain itself does not want them there.

choices.text: Find another path

effects.log: It takes you twice as long to get anywhere now. That is the price of being something men dig holes for.

events.text: A star with a long tail hangs in the east before dawn, night after night. The village below bangs pots and keeps its children indoors. You do not know what it means. Neither, you suspect, do they.

choices.text: Watch it every night until it goes

effects.log: It fades a little each night, like a guest who knows it has stayed too long. Then one night it is gone and the sky looks empty without it.

choices.text: Sleep, and ignore the sky

effects.log: Whatever the star meant, it did not mean you. You sleep well. The village does not.

choices.text: Watch the village instead

effects.log: They argue. Some say war, some say a king will die. An old woman says it means stop arguing. Nobody listens to her.

events.text: The rice paddies are flooded and every frog in the world has come to argue in them. They argue all night. They argue louder when the moon comes up. You were trying to sleep.

choices.text: Listen until the noise becomes music

effects.log: Around midnight it stops being noise. It is a rhythm, older than rice. You sleep inside it like a drum.

choices.text: Go and silence one paddy

effects.log: That paddy falls quiet for a breath. The next one gets louder, to make up for it. You have lost to frogs.

choices.text: Move up the hill

effects.log: It is quieter up the hill. It is also full of owls, who are much quieter and much more interested in you.

events.text: The village has carved two new posts at its gate: great bulging eyes, teeth like a fence, a fierce grin. "Great General Under Heaven," the one on the left says. They are meant to frighten off sickness. And you.

choices.text: Stare back at them all night

effects.log: They do not blink. Neither do you. By morning you have decided they are quite good. Someone worked hard on those teeth.

choices.text: Go past them, slowly, to see what happens

effects.log: Nothing happens. But a dog sees you do it, and in the morning the village is sure the posts have failed. They carve bigger ones.

choices.text: Keep away from the village

effects.log: You stay away all year. The village decides the posts work. They are very proud of the posts.

events.text: An old boar with one broken tusk has come over the ridge. He is enormous and does not care what you are. He wants the oak slope, and he is standing in the middle of it, grunting.

choices.text: Drive him off

ok.log: It is a long, ugly fight in the leaves. He goes, finally, grumbling. The oak slope is quiet again, and you hurt all over.

fail.log: The broken tusk is still a tusk. He opens your side and goes back to his acorns as if you were a bush.

choices.text: Share the slope

effects.log: You take the top, he takes the bottom. Neither of you will admit it is an arrangement. It lasts for years, until he dies.

choices.text: Give him the slope

effects.log: There are other slopes. You go and find one. The boar never knows he won.

events.text: It is acorn season. The squirrels and an old woman with a basket are working the same oak tree from opposite sides. Neither will give way. The squirrels are winning on speed. The old woman has a stick.

choices.text: Watch who wins

effects.log: The old woman. She shakes a branch and the squirrels scatter. She fills her basket, nods to the tree, and goes. The squirrels hold a meeting.

choices.text: Shake a branch for the old woman

effects.log: Acorns rain down. She looks up for a long moment, then picks them up. That winter there is acorn jelly in the village, and a story.

choices.text: Shake a branch for the squirrels

effects.log: The acorns roll down the slope away from her. The squirrels are overjoyed. The old woman looks at the hill like it owes her money.

events.text: You make a sound across the valley, just to hear it. The valley answers. You stop. You make it again. Something answers again, in your voice. For a whole afternoon you think you are not the only one.

choices.text: Keep calling

effects.log: By evening you understand it is the cliff. You keep calling anyway, a little longer. It is good to be answered, even by a cliff.

choices.text: Go and look for it

effects.log: You go half the night to reach the cliff and find nothing but swallows. You call once from the top. The valley answers. You are still alone.

choices.text: Stop, before it stops being yours

effects.log: You leave it there. Somewhere in the valley there is another one of you. You do not need to check.

events.text: The first full moon of the year. On the hill below, the villagers have built a house of pine branches and straw. When the moon clears the ridge they set it alight and dance around it, shouting wishes at the sky.

choices.text: Watch the fire from the dark

effects.log: The fire roars and the sparks go up to the moon. You cannot hear the wishes. You can see the faces. They all wish the same things.

choices.text: Come close enough to feel the heat

effects.log: A girl sees two lights in the dark that are not sparks. She wishes on them. Who knows. It is as good as the moon.

choices.text: Look at the moon instead

effects.log: It looks the same as last year, and the year before. You wish nothing. That may be a kind of wish.

events.text: No rain since summer. One dry wind, one careless spark, and the whole ridge goes up. By night the sky is red and the fire is coming down the slope toward you, faster than it looks.

choices.text: Outrun it over the ridge

ok.log: You cross the ridge with the fire roaring at your back and come down into the cold valley alive, smelling of smoke for a month.

fail.log: The fire turns with the wind and catches you in the pines. You get through, but it takes a long time for the burns to fade.

choices.text: Go down into the stream bed

effects.log: You lie in the cold mud while the fire passes overhead like a train of horses. In the morning the world is black and still smoking.

choices.text: Go to the bare rock above the trees

effects.log: Fire needs fuel. The rock has none. You sit up there coughing and watch the forest burn. It will be back in a lifetime.

events.text: Every spring the swallows come back to the eaves of the same farmhouse. Every spring the farmer's family cheers when they come. It is the luckiest house in the village. You have started to watch for the swallows too.

choices.text: Watch the nest all summer

effects.log: Five chicks. All five fly. The farmer's wife claps each time one leaves the eaves. You feel as if you have won something.

choices.text: Keep the cat away from the eaves

effects.log: The farmer's cat comes to the eaves three nights running and three nights runs away with its hair on end. The swallows raise five.

choices.text: Wonder where they go in winter

effects.log: South, the villagers say, to a country across the sea. You have never seen the sea. It sounds like a lie.

events.text: The arrow comes out of the reeds with no warning. It goes in deep. The shaft snaps when you run, but the iron head stays in you, and it stays there. Behind you a hunter is cursing his luck.

choices.text: Tear at it until it comes out

ok.log: It comes out, with a great deal of you. The hole heals by midsummer. The hunter does not get another shot.

fail.log: It will not come. It has turned in the wound. You give up, panting, and it stays.

choices.text: Leave it and let it close over

effects.log: The flesh closes over the iron. It aches. It will ache, you think, for a long time.

choices.text: Lie in cold mud until the bleeding stops

effects.log: The cold stops the blood. The iron stays. You learn the shape of it, a small hard thing that is now part of you.

events.text: The iron in you aches when the weather is about to turn. Rain, snow, the first frost: you feel each one a day before it comes. The old wound has become the best weather-teller in the valley.

choices.text: Learn to read it

effects.log: Dull is rain. Sharp is frost. A low throb on a clear day means something big, three days off. You are seldom wrong.

choices.text: Rest it through the cold months

effects.log: You stay still all winter and the ache settles to a murmur. The iron and you have reached an understanding.

choices.text: Ignore it and go on as before

effects.log: You will not be ruled by a lump of iron. The iron does not care. It aches anyway.

events.text: After all these years, the old wound itches, then opens, then gives. Something drops into the moss. It is the arrowhead, red with rust, smaller than you remembered. It looks like nothing at all.

choices.text: Bury it

effects.log: You put it in the ground and leave it. A rusty bit of iron under a pine. That is all it ever was.

choices.text: Keep it where you sleep

effects.log: You keep it near. You are not sure why. Some things you carry so long that putting them down feels like a loss.

choices.text: Leave it in the moss for the hunter's grandchildren

effects.log: A boy finds it years later and carries it home. His grandfather looks at it a long while, and says nothing.

events.text: On a winter night you hear a grandmother telling the children about you. You have three heads, she says. You eat children who do not finish their rice. You have been seen in two villages at once, which is true, but not on the same day.

choices.text: Listen to the end

effects.log: In her story you are defeated by a clever girl with a bag of salt. You have never met this girl. You would like to.

choices.text: Pass the window, once

effects.log: Every child in the room finishes their rice for a year. The grandmother is very pleased with herself.

choices.text: Leave before the ending

effects.log: You do not want to know how you die in this one. You have heard four endings already.

events.text: The village has started leaving a table at the edge of the forest for you: rice cakes, a bowl of makgeolli, dried persimmons, all laid out with great care. A brown village dog is sitting in front of it, considering its options.

choices.text: Let the dog have it

effects.log: The dog eats everything, including the paper. The villagers find the plates licked clean and are deeply satisfied. Everyone wins.

choices.text: Take it before the dog does

effects.log: The dog sees you and decides it was never hungry. The rice cakes are good. The makgeolli is better.

choices.text: Leave it all where it is

effects.log: It sits there for three days. The village worries. Then the dog wins. The village is relieved.

events.text: An army comes along the valley road. It takes three days to pass. Spears, banners, carts, horses, men singing, men limping. On the third day there are only stragglers. On the fourth, the dust settles and the road is empty.

choices.text: Watch every man go by

effects.log: You see a boy who should be at home. You see an old man who should be dead. You see a general asleep in a cart. Then you see nothing.

choices.text: Stay hidden and still

effects.log: Thousands of men walk past and not one of them looks up. People who are going to war do not look at trees.

choices.text: Watch for the ones coming back

effects.log: Two years later, a few come back the same way. Fewer than went. Thinner. The boy is among them. You are glad, which surprises you.

events.text: A monk has taken to sitting on the rock across the gorge. He comes at dawn and leaves at dusk. He sits the same hours you do. After a year you are not sure which of you started it.

choices.text: Sit when he sits

effects.log: Two stillnesses, facing. Some days you think he can feel you. Some days you are sure. He never says. Neither do you.

choices.text: Move just as he settles, to test him

effects.log: He does not open his eyes. He smiles, a little. You lose that game every day for a month.

choices.text: Leave a pine cone on his rock one night

effects.log: In the morning he finds it, laughs out loud, and keeps it in his sleeve. He sits a little closer to the edge after that.

events.text: The old mountain god comes down the path with his staff and fan, a white beard to his belt. He sits on a stump and sighs. Your noise is keeping the pilgrims away, he says. His offerings are down by half.

choices.text: Bow to him

effects.log: He is pleased. Old gods are easy to please and hard to impress. He tells you about the pilgrims of four hundred years ago. It takes until dark.

choices.text: Let him work out that your noise is his best story

effects.log: He thinks about it, fanning himself. Then he laughs. The pilgrims come to see where the monster lives, and stay to light incense. He leaves satisfied.

choices.text: Ignore him

effects.log: He talks for an hour anyway. Mountain gods do not need an answer. When he goes, the woods feel faintly scolded.

events.text: The sun is out, and it is raining. The villagers say a fox is getting married. You go to look. There, in the wet grass at the edge of the woods, a line of foxes walks in a solemn procession, one of them wearing a veil of spider silk.

choices.text: Watch from a respectful distance

effects.log: They pass in silence, glittering. The bride glances your way once. The rain stops as the last one goes into the trees.

choices.text: Bow as the bride goes by

effects.log: The whole procession bows back. It is the politest thing that has happened to you in years.

choices.text: Follow to see where the feast is

effects.log: You lose them in the ferns. Somewhere under the hill there is music. You never find the door.

events.text: When you first came, the village below had five roofs. You count them again tonight. Forty-one, a market street, a wall of mud and stone, and a drum tower that booms at dusk. You did not notice it happening.

choices.text: Count them again, slowly

effects.log: Forty-one. And a kiln. And three shrines, one of them, you think, to you. You did not notice that either.

choices.text: Go down at night and go through the new streets

effects.log: A watchman sees something in the alley and drops his lantern. By morning there are forty-one roofs and one new story.

choices.text: Remember the five roofs

effects.log: One of them had a red door. One had a dog that barked at you. You hold them in your mind a while, then let them go.

events.text: In the middle of the day the sun begins to go out. A bite, then half, then a black disc with a ring of fire. In the village they are banging every pot and drum they own. The fire-dogs of the dark kingdom are biting the sun, they say. They must be scared off.

choices.text: Watch the sun come back

effects.log: The bite shrinks. The light returns. The birds, who had gone quiet, all start up at once, embarrassed.

choices.text: Add your own voice to the din

effects.log: Your voice goes across the valley. In the village they bang harder. The sun comes back. They are sure it was you. It might have been.

choices.text: Sleep, since it is suddenly night

effects.log: You doze off. When you wake it is noon again. Nobody else in the world got a nap. You feel ahead.

events.text: The river comes up in the night and keeps coming. In the morning a whole roof goes past you on the brown water, turning slowly. There is a rooster on it, standing very straight, looking furious.

choices.text: Watch the roof out of sight

effects.log: It turns the bend with the rooster still on it, still furious. Downstream, they say later, it fetched up in a field. The rooster lived.

choices.text: Watch the people on the bank

effects.log: They stand in the rain and watch their fields go under. Nobody shouts. An old man holds a child on his shoulders so she can see. You do not know why.

choices.text: Go up high and wait

effects.log: The water goes down in four days. The valley is grey mud for a month. Then it is green, greener than before. The river always gives something back.

events.text: No rain for sixty days. The village has carried a straw dragon to the dry riverbed, and a shaman dances around it, ringing bells. They keep looking toward where you are, as if you could do something about the sky.

choices.text: Watch the rite to the end

effects.log: She dances until she falls. They carry her home. That night a single cloud comes over and drops nine drops. Nobody is sure what to make of it.

choices.text: Keep out of sight; you cannot help

effects.log: There is nothing you can do about the sky, and you know it. Knowing it does not make the waiting easier.

choices.text: Go and lie in the dry riverbed too

effects.log: The stones are hot as a griddle. You lie on them anyway, with the village, and wait. On the seventy-first day it rains.

events.text: A painter has climbed the slope where you were last seen. He sets up his paper, grinds his ink, and paints the monster of the valley from a description by a drunk woodcutter. It looks like a startled cat with a beard.

choices.text: Show yourself, just for a breath

effects.log: He drops the brush. He sits a long time. Then he tears up the cat and starts again, very slowly. It is still wrong. It is closer.

choices.text: Let the cat stand

effects.log: The painting hangs in the magistrate's office for two hundred years. Visitors are told it is you. You find this very relaxing.

choices.text: Watch him paint the mountains instead

effects.log: He gives up on the monster and paints the valley. That one is good. You can see your favourite rock in it.

events.text: The court has sent a troop of tiger-catchers to clear the mountains. Twenty men with spears, bows and dogs, paid by the size of what they kill. They do not know what you are. They know you are big, and that is enough.

choices.text: Lead them in circles until they give up

ok.log: For nine days they chase tracks that loop back on themselves. On the tenth they go home and report the mountain cursed.

fail.log: The dogs are better than the men. They corner you on the scree and the spears come in before you break free.

choices.text: Go deep and wait them out

effects.log: You lie in a cold hollow for a month with nothing to eat. They kill two ordinary tigers and go home happy. You are sorry about the tigers.

choices.text: Frighten the dogs and send them home

effects.log: One look and the dogs bolt down the mountain. Without the dogs the men are just men in the woods. They leave.

events.text: A shaman has come up from the town with peach branches, a sword of bells and a drummer. She is performing a rite to drive you out of the valley. It is a very good rite. Your head rings with it. Your qi is shaking.

choices.text: Endure it

ok.log: You hold your ground through the whole night of drums. At dawn she stops, looks toward you, and bows. She says the spirit is too old to move. She is right.

fail.log: The bells get inside you. By dawn you are sick and shaking and you have moved two valleys away without deciding to.

choices.text: Leave for a season and come back

effects.log: You go. The rite succeeds. The village is happy. When you come back in spring, nobody mentions it, least of all you.

choices.text: Listen to the song inside the rite

effects.log: Under the noise is a very old song about the mountain. It is older than her. It may be older than you. You learn it.

events.text: Smallpox in the village. They call it the honoured guest and treat it with courtesy, so it will leave gently. On the twelfth night they set a straw horse on the road out of town with rice and a lantern. In the morning there are small new graves on the hill.

choices.text: Keep watch over the graves

effects.log: You sit by them all winter. Nothing digs there. In spring the mothers come and find the graves untouched. They do not know why. It is better that way.

choices.text: Watch the straw horse until it is gone

effects.log: Children take the rice. Rain takes the lantern. Wind takes the horse, bit by bit. Whether the guest went with it, you cannot say.

choices.text: Keep far from the village

effects.log: You do not know if it can reach you. You do not find out. The hill has more graves than last year, and you stay away from it.

events.text: The guardian tree in the village square was a sapling when you were young. Now it is the oldest thing in the village, hung with coloured cloth and prayers. Tonight, in a storm, lightning splits it down the middle.

choices.text: Go and look at it in the morning

effects.log: Half of it is black. Half is green. The village is weeping. In the spring the green half puts out leaves, as if nothing happened.

choices.text: Mourn it in your own way

effects.log: You stay up on the hill all night. You do not have many friends older than a hundred years. You have one fewer now.

choices.text: Watch the village decide what to do

effects.log: They argue for a month. In the end they leave it standing, split, and hang the cloth on both halves. Good choice.

events.text: At the first full moon the children write their bad luck on kites and cut the strings. One kite comes down near you, torn, the bad luck still written on it in a child's careful hand.

choices.text: Leave it, bad luck and all

effects.log: It rots into the leaves by summer. Somebody's bad luck is now the forest's. The forest can handle it.

choices.text: Watch the child who comes looking

effects.log: A boy climbs up, finds it, sees what is written on it, and puts it back very carefully where it lay. He is wiser than his parents.

choices.text: Keep it near you

effects.log: You keep someone else's bad luck. It does not seem to do you any harm. Perhaps it was only a cough.

events.text: You sleep well this winter. In the village they say there is thunder under the mountain every night, low and steady. They have sent for a geomancer. The geomancer listens for three nights and says the mountain is breathing.

choices.text: Hold your breath to see what happens

effects.log: The thunder stops. The geomancer goes pale and says the mountain has died. You start again in a hurry. He is paid twice.

choices.text: Sleep on; it is winter

effects.log: You sleep through all of it. By spring the village is proud of its breathing mountain. Pilgrims come to hear it.

choices.text: Move to a quieter place

effects.log: The thunder stops. The geomancer takes credit. He wears the fine robe they give him for years.

events.text: There is a toad that lives under the village granary, and the village treats it like a lord. Never chase the storehouse god away, they say, or the house will fall. The toad knows this. It looks at you as one lord to another.

choices.text: Bow to the toad

effects.log: It blinks, slowly. You are sure that was a bow. The granary is full that year. You will not take credit, and neither will it.

choices.text: Stare it down

effects.log: It does not move all night. Neither do you. At dawn a farmer comes out, sees the toad, bows to it, and does not see you. The toad wins.

choices.text: Watch the granary with it

effects.log: Two lords, one granary. Nothing gets in all winter. Not a rat. Not a weasel. The village thanks the toad.

events.text: Bandits have moved into the pass, into your ground. They are frightened of the stories, so they keep big fires and stay drunk. Tonight they hear something in the trees and come out with torches and spears, yelling to keep their courage up.

choices.text: Show them what lives here

ok.log: They see one glimpse of you in the torchlight and leave the pass by morning without their pots.

fail.log: One of them is braver than the rest, or drunker. His spear finds you before they all run.

choices.text: Let them be; they will go in spring

effects.log: They do. They leave the pass full of broken jars. The magpies take two weeks to sort through it all.

choices.text: Put out their fires, one by one, each night

effects.log: Every fire goes dark. Every night. On the ninth they decide the pass is haunted, and they are not wrong.

events.text: The travellers who cross the pass each add a stone to the cairn under the shrine tree, three times, for a safe road. When you were young, it was knee-high. Now it is taller than a man, and the tree has grown around the bottom stones.

choices.text: Add a stone yourself

effects.log: It is a large stone. In the morning a traveller sees it, a stone no person could lift, and runs the rest of the way.

choices.text: Count the stones

effects.log: You give up at four thousand. Every one is somebody who wanted to get home. Most of them did.

choices.text: Sleep in the shade of it

effects.log: All day people walk past and add stones and bow, and none of them see you. It is like being prayed beside.

events.text: A little girl is crossing the ford alone with a basket of persimmons. She sees you. She does not run. She looks at you for a long moment, then takes out a persimmon, bites it in half, and puts the other half on a stone.

choices.text: Take the half persimmon

effects.log: She nods, very serious, as if a deal has been made. Then she crosses the ford and goes home. You eat the persimmon. It is perfect.

choices.text: Watch her go and leave it

effects.log: She looks back from the far bank, sees it still on the stone, and frowns. Next time, she seems to say. You believe her.

choices.text: Slip away before she can do more

effects.log: When she looks up again you are gone. She shrugs and eats the other half too. Some children are very practical.

events.text: A woman comes to the ford with a basket on her head and a small daughter by the hand. She stops in the middle of the water and points toward you. "There," she says. "Right there. It was looking at me." The daughter does not believe a word.

choices.text: Show yourself, just for the daughter

effects.log: The daughter sees. Her mouth falls open. The woman laughs, delighted, as if she has been proved right after thirty years. She has.

choices.text: Stay hidden; let the mother be believed later

effects.log: They cross. The daughter rolls her eyes. The woman puts half a persimmon on the stone anyway, as if nothing in the world were simpler.

choices.text: Take the persimmon after they cross

effects.log: The woman looks back from the far bank and sees the stone empty. She does not say anything to her daughter. She just smiles all the way home.

events.text: An old woman comes to the ford alone, bent over a stick. She sits on the flat stone and talks to the water, about her daughter, her grandchildren, a bad knee, a good harvest. She does not look for you. She knows you are there. She leaves half a persimmon.

choices.text: Come and sit near her

effects.log: She does not turn. She just keeps talking, a little softer. You stay until the sun goes, and the ford is quiet after.

choices.text: Listen from where you are

effects.log: You hear all of it, a whole life, in an afternoon. When she has finished she pats the stone, as if it were a dog, and goes home.

choices.text: Eat the persimmon after she goes

effects.log: It is perfect, like the first one. You sit at the ford a long time. You never learned her name. She never needed yours.

events.text: A young fox spirit has been going from village to village telling them it is you. It wears a borrowed old man's face, says the mountain is angry, and collects chickens to calm it. The chickens are piling up behind its hollow.
events.arc: The Fox Who Borrows Your Name

choices.text: Go and look at it

effects.log: It sees you and drops its borrowed face. For a long moment it is just a frightened young fox with feathers on its chin.

choices.text: Let it be; it is not hurting anyone

effects.log: Except the chickens. And the villagers' purses. But the stories about you have never been so good.

choices.text: Frighten it out of the valley

effects.log: It runs and does not stop for three mountains. The villages keep their chickens. They decide the mountain is calm again.

events.text: The fox has gone too far. A town has hired a shaman and three hunters with nets to catch the false spirit. Tonight the young fox comes to you, panting, ears flat, and lies down beside you. It has nowhere else to go.
events.arc: The Fox Who Borrows Your Name

choices.text: Hide it until the hunters leave

effects.log: The hunters search for a week. They never look near you. The fox sleeps curled in your shadow and wakes a good deal humbler.

choices.text: Send it away to face them

effects.log: It goes, slowly. You do not know what happened. The town has a fox pelt on the gate that winter. It might not be that fox.

choices.text: Come out where the hunters can see you

effects.log: The hunters see the real thing on the ridge. They look at their small nets. They go home.

events.text: Years later, a grown fox comes to the edge of your ground and sits down at a polite distance. It has a few white hairs at its muzzle now. It sets down a dead pheasant, bows, and leaves without a word.
events.arc: The Fox Who Borrows Your Name

choices.text: Accept the pheasant

effects.log: It comes every autumn for years. A pheasant. A bow. Never a chicken.

choices.text: Follow it and see where it lives now

effects.log: It lives under a shrine in the next valley, honestly, as a fox. The village there leaves it eggs. It looks content.

choices.text: Leave the pheasant for the crows

effects.log: The fox does not mind. It is not about the pheasant. It never was.

events.text: The armies come through again, but their banners are a different colour now. Far to the south, the smoke of the old capital rises for nine days. When the smoke stops, the farmers go back to the fields as if nothing had happened. For them, nothing much has.

choices.text: Watch the smoke until it stops

effects.log: Nine days. A dynasty is a long time for them. For you it is the length of one good sleep. You try to feel it. You do not quite manage.

choices.text: Watch the farmers instead

effects.log: They plant the same rice, the same way, in the same mud. A new king will eat it. The rice does not care.

choices.text: Remember the last time

effects.log: There was a last time, and a time before that. Different colours, the same smoke. You notice you are starting to keep a list.

events.text: Two old immortals have been playing baduk on the flat rock at the summit. A woodcutter stopped to watch them and did not notice when his axe handle rotted. You have been watching for a decade. The game is not yet half done.

choices.text: Keep watching

effects.log: Another decade. White is winning. Then black is. They never look up. You understand three moves. It is enough for a century.

choices.text: Wake the woodcutter and send him home

effects.log: He staggers down the mountain with his rotten axe. His village is a town now. His grandchildren are old. He will be all right. Probably.

choices.text: Knock a stone off the board

effects.log: Both immortals look at you. Then at each other. Then they start the game over, very pleased. You have doubled their afternoon.

events.text: The azaleas come out on the hill, pink as a slap. You realise you have seen this exact hill do this exact thing more than a hundred times. You still stop to look. You wonder when you will stop stopping.

choices.text: Look anyway

effects.log: It is just as good as the first time. Possibly better, because now you know how soon it ends.

choices.text: Count the springs you remember

effects.log: You remember thirty-one clearly. The rest have run together into one long pink spring with you in it.

choices.text: Watch the children who see it for the first time

effects.log: A small boy is running through the flowers with his arms out, shouting. He has never seen anything so good. Neither have you, today.

events.text: Something old and dry passes along the horizon. Where it goes, the streams shrink and the rice yellows. It is Gangcheori, the drought beast, on its long way somewhere. It glances your way. Old things know each other.

choices.text: Meet its gaze

ok.log: It looks at you a long time and then turns off down another valley. Your valley stays green. Theirs does not.

fail.log: Its gaze is a furnace. You feel your qi dry up like a pond in August. It walks on, uninterested. You lie in the shade for a month.

choices.text: Let it pass without a sign

effects.log: It passes. The far hills are brown for a year. You did not choose this, and you could not have stopped it. You are surprised how much that weighs.

choices.text: Watch where it goes

effects.log: West, toward the sea. In the spring, news comes up the road of a terrible drought there. You already knew.

events.text: The Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper keep the length of every life, the old women say. They pray to it for their children. Tonight you count the seven again, as you have a thousand times, and one of them seems to be looking back.

choices.text: Look back

effects.log: Nothing happens. Nothing happens for hours. Then you feel very small, and very counted. The stars do not mention how long you have.

choices.text: Count the old women instead

effects.log: Seven old women in seven yards, all praying at the same stars. You hope at least some of the children get long lives. It seems only fair.

choices.text: Sleep under them

effects.log: Whatever they decide, they will decide it while you sleep. You might as well sleep well.

events.text: A geomancer with a compass has been walking the ridge for a week. Today his men drive an iron stake into the spine of the mountain. You feel it the way a person feels a needle. The earth's qi stops flowing there.

choices.text: Pull the qi around it

ok.log: Slowly, over a winter, you guide the vein around the iron like water around a stone. The mountain breathes again.

fail.log: The vein fights you. For a month you feel sick, as if the stake were in you. Then it settles, crooked.

choices.text: Wait for the iron to rust

effects.log: It takes eighty years. The geomancer is long dead. The day the last of the stake crumbles, the mountain takes a deep breath, and so do you.

choices.text: Watch who comes to pull it out

effects.log: A generation later some villagers find it and dig it out with their bare hands, cursing. They have no idea how grateful you are.

events.text: A scholar is writing the county gazetteer and has come to the entry on you. He reads it aloud as he writes. He has your age wrong by centuries, your colour wrong, and the year you were last seen wrong by a generation.

choices.text: Let the record stand

effects.log: It will be copied, recopied, quoted and printed. Someday someone will argue about it. You find you like being a footnote.

choices.text: Appear on the slope as he finishes

effects.log: He looks up from the page, sees you, and slowly crosses out one line. Then another. Then he puts his brush down and stares for an hour.

choices.text: Listen to the rest of the gazetteer

effects.log: It has the rivers wrong too, and two of the mountains. But it has the name of every village, and every good well. You learn a lot.

events.text: The giant grandmother comes over the far range with her skirt hitched up and full of rocks. She is building something, she says, or she was, she has forgotten what. She sits down on a mountain to rest, and the mountain is a bit lower after.

choices.text: Keep her company

effects.log: She talks about the world when it was soft, when you could pinch up a mountain like dough. She calls you young. It is very pleasant.

choices.text: Help her remember what she was building

effects.log: A bridge, you work out, to the islands. She laughs at herself and goes off to find more rocks. It will never be finished. She does not mind.

choices.text: Keep out of her way

effects.log: She drops a rock as she goes. It is the size of a temple. A village will be built against it, and argue for centuries about where it came from.

events.text: The old pine on the eastern ridge has finally fallen. It was the last living thing that remembered you when you were young. The rest went long ago: every crane, every boar, every monk, every child at the ford. Now the pine.

choices.text: Go and lie beside it

effects.log: Its trunk is hollow. Its needles are still green at the top. You stay for a season. Moss starts on it. That is how it will go.

choices.text: Look for something young to know

effects.log: There is a pine seedling at the edge of the root ball, no taller than a thumb. You decide it will do.

choices.text: Accept it and go on

effects.log: You were always going to outlive everything. Knowing it is not the same as watching it. You watch it, all the same.

events.text: A winter so cold the sea freezes at the shore and the birds fall out of the trees. The villages burn their fences, then their doors. Even you feel it, deep, in places you did not know could be cold.

choices.text: Endure it alone

effects.log: You sit through it like a stone. When the spring comes you are thinner and stiller and older than you were. Everyone is.

choices.text: Watch the village survive it

effects.log: They pack every family into the three warmest houses. They share everything. Two old people die. Everyone else lives, crowded and cross and alive.

choices.text: Drive a deer herd toward the village

effects.log: A herd comes down the valley in the snow, right to their fences. Nobody asks why. In spring they leave a bowl of rice on the hill.

events.text: The clouds have been gathering over you for three days and nowhere else. Tonight the thunder starts, and it is not random. It is looking for you. Heaven tests the old things, now and then, to see if they still deserve to be.

choices.text: Face it in the open

ok.log: Nine strikes. You take every one. At dawn the clouds part and the sky is very clean. Something up there has crossed you off a list.

fail.log: The fifth strike puts you down. The sixth through ninth hit a body that is barely there. You live. It takes a long time to feel alive.

choices.text: Go to ground and let it rage

effects.log: The lightning splits rocks all around you. It does not find you. Heaven is not pleased, but heaven is patient. It will try again.

choices.text: Draw it toward the iron in the old mine

effects.log: The bolts follow the iron. The hill glows all night. In the morning there is a lake where the mine was. You did not know you could do that.

events.text: Every spring now, pilgrims climb the mountain with lanterns to the spot where you were seen, long ago. They bow there. They tie ribbons. You have not been near that spot in generations. You watch them from somewhere else.

choices.text: Go and stand where they bow

effects.log: They see nothing but a shadow on the rocks. It is enough. One old woman cries. You are not sure you deserve it. You stand there anyway.

choices.text: Watch from your own place

effects.log: They bow to an empty rock with total sincerity. It occurs to you that they might be praying to something you used to be.

choices.text: Watch the children on the pilgrimage

effects.log: The children are bored. They throw stones and chase each other and get scolded. One of them stops, looks right at you, and waves.

events.text: The children in the town have a game. One child is you, and the rest chase it. The child who is you has to roar and wave its arms and hide behind the well. When caught, it falls down dead with great drama.

choices.text: Watch a whole afternoon of it

effects.log: You are slain eleven times before dinner. Some of the deaths are quite moving. One girl is very good at being you.

choices.text: Rustle the bushes when they come close

effects.log: They scream and scatter. Then they come back, and do it again, and again. You have joined the game, and the game knows it.

choices.text: Watch the adults watching them

effects.log: The parents used to play it too. Their parents too. You realise the game is older than the town. You are older than the game.

events.text: Famine again. The rice is gone and the barley is green. People are boiling pine bark. A thin family is searching the edge of the forest, coming closer to you each day.

choices.text: Drive a deer toward them

effects.log: A young buck comes down out of the trees as if pushed, right into their path. They do not ask questions. Neither does the buck, now.

choices.text: Show them where the wild greens are

effects.log: Something moves in the brush. They follow it to a hollow full of wild garlic and fern. They pick until dark and bow to the forest.

choices.text: Stay out of their way

effects.log: Hungry people are dangerous. You let them pass. The barley ripens in nine days. Two of them are alive to eat it.

events.text: A cultivator has climbed the mountain to find you. He is very good, the best of his age, and he has come to test himself against something older than his sect. He draws his sword and waits, polite and terrifying.

choices.text: Give him his test

ok.log: It takes all afternoon. When it is over, he sheathes his sword and bows to the ground, shaking. He has learned what he came to learn: he is young.

fail.log: He is better than you thought. He goes home with a story and a cut of your qi. You go deep and heal for years.

choices.text: Leave before he can begin

effects.log: He waits a month. He is very patient. In the end he carves a poem into the rock about the thing that would not fight him, and goes.

choices.text: Watch him wait

effects.log: He stands perfectly still for nine days, sword out. On the tenth he laughs, bows to the empty slope, and leaves. You think he understood.

events.text: For as long as you can remember the temple bell in the valley has rung at dawn. You wake to it. You have woken to it since before the town had a wall. This morning, it does not ring.

choices.text: Go down to find out why

effects.log: The bell is gone. The army took it for its bronze, to make cannon. The monks are sweeping the empty bell pavilion. They sweep all morning.

choices.text: Wait for it tomorrow

effects.log: It does not ring tomorrow. Or the next day. You keep waking at the right time, for years, for nothing. Then one day you do not.

choices.text: Hum the note yourself, at dawn

effects.log: In the valley they hear it, faint, every dawn. They say the bell's ghost rings. The monks know better. They bow to the mountain.

events.text: At dawn, a crow with three legs lands on the rock beside you and looks you over. It is the crow of the sun, the stories say. It looks unimpressed. It looks at the sun, then at you, then back at the sun.

choices.text: Look unimpressed back

effects.log: You stare. It stares. It makes a small noise like a laugh and goes off to do whatever the sun needs. You feel you won.

choices.text: Ask it nothing; wait

effects.log: It stays until noon, warming your rock. When it goes the rock is hot for a week. You do not understand what happened. That is probably correct.

choices.text: Follow its flight with your eyes

effects.log: It flies straight into the sun. You blink for an hour afterward. Some things are not for watching.

events.text: The sky in the north goes dark at noon. A week later grey ash falls like snow on a summer day. The leaves go grey. The rice goes grey. The old people say a mountain far away has torn itself open.

choices.text: Watch the summer that never comes

effects.log: It is cold in July. Nothing ripens. You have never seen the world forget its seasons. It frightens you more than any hunter did.

choices.text: Shelter the young animals of the valley

effects.log: You keep a hollow clear of ash and the deer and the boar shelter there with you. Nobody eats anybody. It is a strange year.

choices.text: Sleep until it passes

effects.log: You sleep two years. When you wake the ash is soil and the soil is green. It is the best rice in a hundred years.

events.text: You sleep for ten years. When you wake, moss has grown on the rock beside you and the path has moved. The people walking it go around the place where you lie, in a careful loop, without knowing why.

choices.text: Get up and see what changed

effects.log: A new bridge. A new shrine. A new magistrate, mostly the same as the old one. Ten years, and the most interesting thing is a bridge.

choices.text: Stay and watch the loop

effects.log: Children step off the path to go round you. Old men too. A cart goes round. Something in them knows. You are pleased about this.

choices.text: Go back to sleep

effects.log: Ten more years. Why not. The world will still be there. It is very good at being there.

events.text: Monks have built a small hall on the slope where you were seen. On the wall is a painting of you. It is completely wrong. Too many eyes, a very friendly smile, and a halo. They light incense to it every morning.

choices.text: Watch them build

effects.log: Four monks and a carpenter, one summer. They sing while they work, the same song, badly. By autumn there is a roof.

choices.text: Stare at the painting

effects.log: The smile is the worst part. You have never smiled like that in your life. You suspect they have improved you.

choices.text: Stay away from it

effects.log: It is their hall, not yours. You let them have it. In a few years it falls down in a storm, unvisited.

events.text: The little hall is a temple now, with a gate, a pagoda and a festival every spring. Hundreds come. They hang lanterns on the trees, eat rice cakes, buy charms with your face on them. Your face is still smiling.

choices.text: Watch the festival from the ridge

effects.log: The lanterns go up after dark like a field of slow fireflies. You watch until the last one goes out. You feel, oddly, like a host.

choices.text: Go close enough for the incense

effects.log: The incense smells of pine and old ash. Somebody's grandmother bows to the hillside where you are standing, and does not know.

choices.text: Watch the old monk who sweeps the yard

effects.log: He sweeps the yard every morning, all of it, the same way. He is the only one who does not look toward the hillside. He is the only one who knows.

events.text: War comes over the mountains. The temple burns in a single night. In the morning there is only one old monk left, sweeping the ash from the stone steps. When he is done, he plants a pine sapling where the gate was.

choices.text: Watch over the sapling

effects.log: It grows. The monk does not. When he dies, a few villagers bury him beside it. The pine is huge now. Nobody remembers the temple.

choices.text: Mourn the painting

effects.log: It was wrong. It was friendlier than you. You find you miss it.

choices.text: Sit with the old monk

effects.log: He sits on the steps and talks to the hillside, about the temple, about the war, about his knees. He is talking to you. You are fairly sure of it.

events.text: A new star has appeared in the east, brighter than any other, where there was nothing last night. The court astronomers are on their roofs. In the villages they say it means a sage is born. The star does not say anything.

choices.text: Watch it every night

effects.log: It burns steady and white. You start to plan your nights around it. You have not done that since you were young.

choices.text: Watch the astronomers on their roof

effects.log: They sketch it, measure it, argue, and write a long report for the king. You admire them. They are trying to understand something they cannot touch. So are you.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: A star is a star. You sleep. It burns for months, they say, and goes. You do not miss it, because you never looked.

events.text: The guest star is fading. Every night it is a little dimmer. The astronomers are still up there, still writing. The sage they promised has not appeared. Or perhaps he is a baby somewhere, and has not said anything yet.

choices.text: Watch it until it is gone

effects.log: One night you cannot find it. The sky looks the same as it did. You know better. It will never look quite the same to you again.

choices.text: Look for the baby

effects.log: There are a great many babies. All of them shout. None of them seem especially wise. You decide to come back in a few years.

choices.text: Watch the old astronomer close his book

effects.log: He writes the last line, sits back, and looks at the sky for a while with nothing in his hands. You know exactly how he feels.

events.text: You look up at the peak you have looked at every morning for ages, and it is lower. Not much. A man's height, perhaps. The wind has been taking it, one grain at a time, and you were watching the whole time.

choices.text: Measure it against the stars

effects.log: A man's height in all that time. You do the sum. In a long time it will be a hill. You will see that. The idea is very strange.

choices.text: Feel the wind work on it

effects.log: You sit on the summit through a storm. You feel each grain go. It does not hurt the mountain. You are not sure about you.

choices.text: Laugh at it

effects.log: You have outlasted a part of a mountain. That is the most ridiculous thing you have ever accomplished. You laugh until the birds leave.

events.text: The salt marsh where the herons used to fish is rice fields now. The shore is a day's walk further out. The village that was a fishing village grows rice and tells its children it always did.

choices.text: Go to the new shore

effects.log: There is a new marsh there, and new herons, and a new fishing village. It is all happening again, a day further out.

choices.text: Remember the herons

effects.log: There was one with a bent leg who fished the same pool for years. You have not thought of it in centuries. You think of it now.

choices.text: Watch the old farmer who still mends a net

effects.log: He has a fishing net he has never used, from his grandfather. He mends it every winter. He does not know why. You do.

events.text: The people in the valley have a new name for you this century. It is one of many you know of. The first was the noise a child made. One meant thief. One meant grandmother. This one means the old neighbour.

choices.text: Try the new name on

effects.log: The old neighbour. You like it. You have been called worse, and for longer. You think it may stick.

choices.text: Remember them all in order

effects.log: You can still recite them all. Every one is a generation of people trying to describe you to their children. None of them were wrong, exactly.

choices.text: Wonder what you call yourself

effects.log: You do not have a name for yourself. You never needed one. That might be the oldest thing about you.

events.text: Four hundred years ago a ferryman told a joke on the river while you were listening from the bank. You did not understand it. Today, for no reason at all, while watching a cloud, you suddenly do.

choices.text: Laugh

effects.log: You laugh so hard the birds lift off the whole hillside. It was a very good joke. The ferryman would be delighted.

choices.text: Look for the ferryman's descendants

effects.log: There is a man selling rice wine by the bridge with the same nose. You consider the joke, and him. It is enough to know he exists.

choices.text: Wonder what else you missed

effects.log: Four hundred years for one joke. You think about everything else you have half-heard. You may have a great deal of laughing ahead of you.

events.text: A messenger of the Jade Emperor comes down a beam of light with a scroll, looks at you, checks the scroll, looks at you again, and frowns. It appears there has been a mistake about which valley. He apologises at great length.

choices.text: Let him read you the scroll anyway

effects.log: It is a summons for somebody else to a banquet in heaven. It sounds tedious. You are glad it was not for you.

choices.text: Point him to the next valley

effects.log: He bows three times and goes off in the right direction. A week later a famous hermit in the next valley vanishes. You know where he went.

choices.text: Ask him nothing and watch him go

effects.log: Heaven, it seems, is as muddled as earth. You find that comforting. You have been worried about heaven for centuries.

events.text: A messenger turtle from the Dragon King of the Eastern Sea crawls up the valley, very slowly, with news. One of the other old ones is gone. One you met once, long ago, and never forgot.

choices.text: Mourn in silence for a season

effects.log: You stay still all autumn. The leaves fall on you. There are fewer of the old ones every century. Some day there will be one.

choices.text: Ask the turtle how it happened

effects.log: Slowly, as turtles do, it tells you. Tired, it says. Just tired, after a long time. It does not sound so bad.

choices.text: Send the turtle back with nothing

effects.log: It crawls away down the valley. It will take it a year to reach the sea. By then it will be the old news, and you will have made your peace.

events.text: Generations of children have run from you. Today one does not. A small boy walks straight up to you, puts his hand on you, laughs, and runs home to tell his mother, who does not believe him.
events.arc: The Child Who Is Not Afraid

choices.text: Hold still for him

effects.log: His hand was warm and sticky with something sweet. Nobody has done that in ages. You do not move for an hour after he goes.

choices.text: Watch him grow up

effects.log: He becomes a woodcutter, then an old woodcutter, and every time he passes your hill he raises a hand. You count the times. Six hundred and twelve.

choices.text: Let it be a dream to him

effects.log: By his tenth birthday he thinks he dreamed it. You do not mind. You were somebody's good dream.

events.text: Tonight you feel the whole land at once: every mountain vein, every spring, every deep river of qi under the peninsula, beating slow, like a sleeping heart. You have never felt it so clearly.

choices.text: Breathe with it until dawn

effects.log: For one night you are not separate from the land. In the morning you are, again. But you know where you belong.

choices.text: Follow one vein as far as you can

effects.log: You follow it south three hundred li to a small spring at a temple. A monk is drinking from it, with his eyes closed. You let go.

choices.text: Listen for anything wrong in it

effects.log: There is a knot in the east, an old wound in the land where something was dug out. You feel it like your own. You will watch it.

events.text: Nothing happens this year. No war, no famine, no hunters, no gods. The rice grows. The rain comes on time. A few people are born, a few die, a dog has puppies. You watch all of it.

choices.text: Enjoy it

effects.log: It is the best year in a century. Nobody will remember it, because nothing happened. You will.

choices.text: Wait for the catch

effects.log: There is no catch. You are so used to catches that you spend the whole year waiting. It is a little embarrassing.

choices.text: Watch the puppies

effects.log: There are five. One is brave, one is greedy, one sleeps all day. You decide the sleepy one is the wisest. It grows up to be the village's best dog.

events.text: You try to remember the first human face you ever saw. It was a long time ago. A hunter, or a child, or a woman at a well. You remember the light. You remember the fear. You cannot remember the face.

choices.text: Keep trying

effects.log: Days of it. You remember a scar on a hand, a red cord, a voice. The face stays gone. Perhaps it was only ever those things.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: Some things wear away like the peak. That one did. You let it.

choices.text: Remember the last face instead

effects.log: A girl selling chestnuts, yesterday. You keep that one. You do not know how long you will have it.

events.text: The forest at the foot of your mountain is a city now. Walls, gates, palaces, ten thousand roofs. At night the lights go up the slope almost to where you lie. They have no idea there is anyone up here.

choices.text: Watch the lights all night

effects.log: They go out one by one, from the bottom up. By dawn there are only the night watchmen and you. You feel like a night watchman too.

choices.text: Go along the city wall at night

effects.log: A gatekeeper sees a great dark shape at the wall and closes his eyes and counts to a hundred. When he opens them, there is nothing. He tells no one.

choices.text: Remember the forest

effects.log: There was a stream where the main gate is. An oak where the palace is. You know where every one of them was. Nobody else does.

events.text: You turned over in your sleep and a landslide came down the north face. In the capital, the astronomers have written it down as an omen. A minister has resigned. You did not mean anything by it.

choices.text: Lie very still for a while

effects.log: You keep still for a year. Nothing slides. The court decides heaven is pleased. A new minister is appointed. You are careful about your sleep.

choices.text: Find it funny

effects.log: A man lost his post because you had an itch. You find it funnier than you should. Heaven, presumably, is laughing too.

choices.text: Go and look at the landslide

effects.log: It has opened a seam of white stone in the mountain. In a hundred years a temple will be built from it, by people who think it was a sign.

events.text: On the sunny slope facing you, one family has buried its dead for twenty-two generations. You know every mound. The farmer who drank too much. The midwife. The boy who drowned. The man who planted the chestnut tree.

choices.text: Keep watch over them on the festival day

effects.log: They come with food and wine and bow at every mound. You watch the young ones bow at the drowned boy without knowing who he was. You know.

choices.text: Remember them in order

effects.log: Twenty-two generations. You could tell their story better than they can. You never will. It is not that kind of story.

choices.text: Watch the newest mound

effects.log: A grandmother. She used to sing while she cut the grass on the other graves. Now her great-grandson does it, badly, without the song.

events.text: In the night the ground shakes, then shakes harder. Rocks come down. The river jumps its banks. Below, the villages are screaming in the dark. The earth itself is trying to throw you off.

choices.text: Hold the slope above the village

ok.log: The landslide breaks around you like water around a rock. The village below wakes to find a wall of boulders stopped just above their roofs.

fail.log: The mountain is stronger than you. It carries you down with it, and you lie under the rubble for a season before you can move.

choices.text: Go to bare rock and ride it out

effects.log: You wait. The shaking goes on and on, then stops. In the morning the valley is a different shape. You will have to learn it again.

choices.text: Listen to the earth while it moves

effects.log: Under the terror there is something else: the earth adjusting itself, like a sleeper turning. You learn more in one night than in a century.

events.text: A pine seed caught on you a hundred years ago, when you lay down in a new place. It is a tree now, a tall one, exactly where you slept that winter. You have been followed, very slowly, by a forest.

choices.text: Sit under it

effects.log: It shades you as if it knows. It does not. It is a pine. But you are quite fond of it.

choices.text: Look for others

effects.log: You find a line of them across three valleys, each where you rested. A map of your life, in pines. Somebody should write it down.

choices.text: Wonder what else you have left behind

effects.log: Stories, mostly. And pines. And one very confused geomancer. It is not a bad legacy.

events.text: It is a very long afternoon. You have counted the stones on the hill. Twelve thousand and four. You count them again. Twelve thousand and five. Someone, at some point, added a stone.

choices.text: Find the new stone

effects.log: It takes all evening. It is a small round one from the river, placed carefully on a ledge. A child, you think. You leave it exactly where it is.

choices.text: Count something else

effects.log: Clouds: thirty-one. Birds: too many. Thoughts: one, over and over, which is that you are bored. It is a strange luxury.

choices.text: Sleep through the rest of the afternoon

effects.log: When you wake it is evening, and the whole thing is solved. Afternoons always end. That is the one thing you are sure of.

events.text: On the seventh night of the seventh month every magpie in the land is gone, flown up to make a bridge across the River of Heaven, so the Herdboy and the Weaver Girl can meet. By morning it is raining: their tears, the old women say.

choices.text: Watch the sky all night

effects.log: The two stars draw a little closer. Or you imagine it. You have watched it for so long you can no longer tell.

choices.text: Look for the magpies in the morning

effects.log: They come back with bald patches on their heads, from the lovers stepping on them. The children point. The magpies look smug.

choices.text: Sit in the rain

effects.log: Their tears are warm. Once a year, for thousands of years. You feel you are in good company.

events.text: A travelling troupe comes to the town market and performs a mask dance about you. The dancer who plays you has a huge red mask with gold eyes and stamps around, roaring. The crowd loves it. The real you is on the hill.

choices.text: Watch the whole play

effects.log: You are defeated in the last act by a monk with a fan. The crowd cheers. You find you are cheering too, in your way.

choices.text: Watch the dancer after the show

effects.log: Behind the wagon, mask off, the dancer is an old man rubbing his knees. He has played you for forty years. He is better at it than you are.

choices.text: Make a sound at the climax

effects.log: Just as the monk lifts his fan, a long low sound comes from the hill. The crowd freezes. The dancer, a professional, roars back. Best show of the year.

events.text: In the city a drum is beaten at dusk to close the gates, as it has been for five hundred years. You have heard every one. Tonight the drummer misses a beat. Somebody new. You find yourself waiting for the next one.

choices.text: Count the beats with him

effects.log: He finds his rhythm by the twentieth. By next year he will be perfect. Then he will grow old. Then someone new will miss a beat.

choices.text: Remember the first drummer

effects.log: A big woman with a laugh like a cart falling over. She beat it for years. She would have scolded this one.

choices.text: Let the beat put you to sleep

effects.log: Five hundred years of dusk. It is the most reliable thing you know. You sleep, and the gates close, and everything is in its place.

events.text: After a great flood the river does not go back. It has cut a new bed a mile to the west and left its old one behind: a long curve of sand and stones and stranded pools, with fish dying in them.

choices.text: Follow the old bed

effects.log: You follow it end to end. Every bend is one you knew. It feels like walking through an empty house.

choices.text: Watch the new river find its way

effects.log: It is wild and brown and unsure of itself. It will take a century to settle. You have time.

choices.text: Let it go; rivers move

effects.log: It is only a river. There will be others. You find you do not believe yourself, quite.

events.text: The old riverbed is a village now. Good soil, flat ground, a well that never runs dry. The people who live there do not know there was ever a river. Their children play in what used to be the deepest pool.

choices.text: Watch the children play

effects.log: They dig in the sand and find river stones, smooth as eggs. They do not wonder why. You almost wish they would.

choices.text: Remember the river in their place

effects.log: Where the headman's house is, there was a whirlpool. Where the shrine is, an otter's slide. You lay the river over the village in your mind, and both are real.

choices.text: Watch the river, a mile off, for signs

effects.log: It has settled. It looks content. But every spring flood, it leans a little east. You know that lean.

events.text: A great flood again, and the river comes back for its bed. It pours down the old curve as if it had never left. The village is in the way. You watch the people carry what they can, old women on their sons' backs, up the hill.

choices.text: Watch them to safety

effects.log: They all reach the hill. They stand in the rain and watch their village go. Then, because they are human, they start planning a new one.

choices.text: Watch the river come home

effects.log: It fills every bend exactly. It knew the way. It was only waiting. You think you understand rivers now, a little.

choices.text: Wonder which of you will move next

effects.log: The river has gone and come back in the time you have sat here. You are starting to suspect that you are the one thing in this valley that does not move.
